sources.entry: Brooklyn - Screensaver inspired by Apple's Event on October 30, 2018.

summary.one_liner: A macOS screen saver that replays the animations from Apple's October 30, 2018 event, created by Pedro Carrasco; the project is no longer actively maintained.
summary.what_it_does: Brooklyn is a screen saver for macOS based on the animations shown at Apple's October 30, 2018 special event held at the Brooklyn Academy of Music. It runs without an internet connection and offers light and dark themes. Users can choose which animations to show, set how many times each one loops, and randomize the playback order. It can be installed manually from a downloaded .saver file or through Homebrew, and the README includes a Terminal command to set it as the active screen saver. The README says the project is not actively maintained and that bug fixes are available for a fee by contacting the author.
use_cases: Replace the macOS screen saver with Apple event-style animations
Run an offline animated screen saver on a Mac
Install a screen saver via Homebrew cask
Choose and loop specific screen saver animations
how_to_run: Manual: download Brooklyn.saver, double-click it, and allow it under Security & Privacy > General > Open Anyway
defaults -currentHost write com.apple.screensaver moduleDict -dict moduleName Brooklyn path "$HOME/Library/Screen Savers/Brooklyn.saver"
If blocked on macOS Big Sur or later: sudo xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ~/"Library/Screen Savers/Brooklyn.saver"
notable: Works offline with no internet connection needed
Per-animation selection, loop count, and random ordering
Installable via Homebrew cask with --no-quarantine flag
caveats: Not actively maintained; bug fixes are offered for a fee
Requires OS X El Capitan (10.11) or later
Unsigned app may be blocked by macOS and need manual quarantine removal, especially on Big Sur
